entries.subject: Galeopterus variegatus
entries.title: A small wave
entries.body: I tried to give a discreet little wave. Opened an entire side of myself. The neighbor thought I was leaving.

image.sceneMatch: Colugo clings to a trunk with one forelimb extended and the membrane visibly folded along its side. The little wave is fictional, using that exact anatomy.

provenance.title: File:Kaguaani 02.jpg
provenance.creator: Nina Holopainen
provenance.sourceDescription: Cynocephalus variegatus. Colugo is the other name. And kaguan. Malayan flying lemur.

entries.payoff: Small social gesture accidentally opens a large gliding surface.

entries.subject: Galeopterus variegatus
entries.title: A dream
entries.body: I dreamed I was falling. Woke up gripping bark with every claw. Then remembered that later I would have to do the falling on purpose.

image.sceneMatch: Close portrait shows spread claws firmly gripping a trunk. Dream and waking memory are fiction; red eye shine is photographic flash, not the character's natural eye color.

provenance.title: File:Sunda Flying Lemur (Galeopterus variegatus) (15503712798).jpg
provenance.creator: Bernard DUPONT from FRANCE
provenance.sourceDescription: Permai Rainforest Resort, Santubong Peninsula North of Kuching, Sarawak, MALAYSIA

entries.payoff: Sleep treats as danger what waking life deliberately requires.

entries.subject: Galeopterus variegatus
entries.title: The extra journey
entries.body:
There was no reason to cross back. I had eaten. The bark was good. Nobody was bothering me.

I climbed anyway.

At the top I spread myself and left. The air pulled tight beneath me. For a little while I had no weight against my feet and no leaf in my mouth and nothing to hold.

I reached the other trunk much too pleased with myself. Clung there, pretending I had come to inspect something.

There was a leaf. I inspected it. Entirely ordinary.

Then I climbed that tree and went back.

I used to think all the gaps in the forest were an inconvenience. Tonight I crossed the same one six times. Ate the leaf on the fifth trip so that I would have an explanation.

image.sceneMatch: Colugo holds a trunk with its large folded gliding membrane visible. Repeated pleasure glides are recalled action, not claimed airborne footage.

entries.payoff: Repeated unnecessary gliding becomes pleasure with a flimsy dietary excuse.

entries.subject: Galeopterus variegatus
entries.title: Please don't
entries.body: I am not stuck. I live vertically. Please stop offering me help from the ground.

image.sceneMatch: Colugo clings vertically to a large trunk, directly supporting the misunderstanding about being stuck.

entries.payoff: Ground-dweller misreads a successful vertical life as a rescue situation.

entries.subject: Daubentonia madagascariensis
entries.title: Reach
entries.body: Someone asked why I needed such a long finger. I was halfway inside a flower. I let them work it out.

image.sceneMatch: Aye-aye holds and reaches into a banana inflorescence. The gesture and specialized finger are central; no grubs or prey are shown or invented.

entries.payoff: Specialized reach makes the intrusive anatomical question answer itself.

entries.subject: Daubentonia madagascariensis
entries.title: The other tapping
entries.body:
Something was tapping farther along the branch. I stopped. It stopped.

I tapped twice. Two taps came back. I went around the trunk. Nobody there. Returned to my branch. Three taps this time. Three back.

I was beginning to feel rather good about having invented a conversation.

Then the other aye-aye came into view. He had been going around the tree the other way.

We stared at each other. He tapped once. I tapped once.

He climbed down. I stayed.

A little later the tapping started below me. Not an answer this time. His own uneven rhythm. I could hear him getting farther away.

I did not follow. But I stopped eating until I couldn't hear it anymore.

image.sceneMatch: Aye-aye sits among branching limbs with its hands visible. The second aye-aye and tapping encounter are remembered fiction, not visibly documented.

entries.payoff: An imagined dialogue becomes a real meeting, then attentive listening without pursuit.

entries.subject: Daubentonia madagascariensis
entries.title: The forest at night
entries.body: I was trying to listen to the forest. My own chewing was in the way. I stopped. The forest turned out to be mostly other people chewing.

image.sceneMatch: Aye-aye handles a banana inflorescence; feeding, large ears and night surroundings support the listening-versus-chewing scene.

entries.payoff: Quiet reveals a shared bodily occupation rather than majestic silence.

entries.subject: Daubentonia madagascariensis
entries.title: Anybody in?
entries.body: I knocked. Nobody answered. This has never stopped me.

image.sceneMatch: Aye-aye clings beside large jackfruit. Knocking is fictional exploratory behavior; no hollow cavity or insect is asserted to be visible.

entries.payoff: A polite gesture cannot conceal the intention to investigate the fruit.

entries.subject: Saiga tatarica tatarica
entries.title: At the water
entries.body: I lowered my face to drink and watched my reflection turn into a nose with horns. Lifted my head. Tried a different angle. The water is being very consistent about this.

image.sceneMatch: Adult horned male saiga wades in shallow water with its distinctive nose visible. The imagined reflection is not resolved in this image.

provenance.title: File:Saiga antelope at the Stepnoi Sanctuary.jpg

provenance.sourceDescription: Wild saiga antelope, Saiga tatarica tatarica visiting a waterhole at the Stepnoi Sanctuary, Astrakhan Oblast, Russia.

entries.payoff: Repeated angles cannot escape the nose that defines the face.

entries.subject: Saiga tatarica tatarica
entries.title: Winter face
entries.body: My winter coat is coming in. I tried to look windswept. I look recently excavated.

image.sceneMatch: Adult horned male saiga wears a pale thick coat and dark neck hair in an open sparse landscape, supporting the winter appearance.

provenance.creator: Лариса Артемьева
provenance.sourceDescription: Russian Saiga (Saiga tatarica tatarica) in Russia

entries.payoff: Attempted windswept elegance becomes an unearthed appearance.

entries.subject: Saiga tatarica tatarica
entries.title: Excellent concealment
entries.body: Mother walked straight past me. I had never hidden so well. For one glorious moment I was invisible. Then I squeaked.

image.sceneMatch: Very young saiga lies folded against the ground with its legs tucked near its face. Mother and the squeak are fictional remembered events.

provenance.title: File:Saiga tatarica tatarica 128448849.jpg
provenance.creator: Лариса Артемьева
provenance.sourceDescription: Russian Saiga (Saiga tatarica tatarica) in Russia

entries.payoff: Pride in concealment lasts only until attachment becomes urgent.

entries.subject: Saiga tatarica tatarica
entries.title: The waiting
entries.body:
Mother told me to stay down. I put my legs under me. There seemed to be too many, but eventually they fitted.

She went away through the grass. I kept my head low. An insect climbed over my foot. I let it. I was doing this properly.

I could hear the others moving. Then only the grass.

I had several questions. Whether she knew which patch I was in. Whether I would know her when she came back. Whether the insect had gone or was now somewhere more important.

I waited until I could not possibly wait any longer.

When I opened my eyes, her nose was against my ear. I had slept through being brave.

I stood up too quickly and had to find my legs again. She waited.

image.sceneMatch: Young saiga lies low with folded legs in sparse grass. The source does not establish its sex; it illustrates an adult male narrator's invented early memory.

provenance.title: File:Saiga tatarica tatarica 127195486.jpg
provenance.creator: Лариса Артемьева
provenance.sourceDescription: Russian Saiga (Saiga tatarica tatarica) in Russia

entries.payoff: The frightening vigil passes in sleep; the mother's patient return lets the calf unfold.
